title: Selective Cell Elimination from Mixed 3D Culture Using a Near Infrared Photoimmunotherapy Technique
protocol: Prepare mAb of interest at a concentration between 2-5 mg/ml in a 0.1 M Na2HPO4 solution (pH 8.6).
Mix 6.8 nmol of mAb with 30.8 nmol of IR700 in the same buffer and incubate for 1 hour at room temperature, covered with aluminum foil.
Wash a PD-10 column twice with 15 ml PBS each time.
Load the conjugated sample onto the PD-10 column for purification using PBS elution according to manufacturer's instructions.
Elute the purified mixture along the band color of IR700, collecting typically between 2.5 ml and 4.4 ml fractions for a 300 μl sample.
Determine the protein concentration with Coomassie staining by measuring absorbance at 595 nm using a spectrophotometer.
Measure the concentration of IR700 at 689 nm to confirm the number of fluorophore molecules conjugated per mAb molecule.
Store the purified and concentrated mAb-IR700 conjugate at 4 °C after determining its protein concentration.
Apply sterile water into the plate reservoir section of hanging drop plates.
Prepare various ratios of A431-luc-GFP cells and 3T3-RFP cells, with each sample containing 5,000 cells suspended in 50 µl of culture media.
Incubate the mix for 5-7 days in a humidified incubator at 37 °C and 5% carbon dioxide.
Change the culture media every 2 days.
Handle the plate gently to prevent drops containing cells from falling off easily before forming 3D shapes.
Observe the morphology and size of the spheroids using an inverted brightfield microscope at 10X - 40X magnification.
Ensure that the diameter of the spheroid is around 400-600 µm after 7 days of incubation in the 96 well hanging drop plate.
Change the media of the hanging drop plates to 10 µg/ml antibody-photoabsorber conjugate (APC) containing media.
Incubate for 6 hours in a humidified incubator at 37 °C and 5% carbon dioxide.
Incubate the spheroid for 6 hours.
Wash the spheroid twice with fresh phenol red free culture medium.
Transfer the spheroid to a glass-bottomed 50 mm dish containing 100 µl of fresh phenol red free culture media using a sterile pipette tip with the tip cut off.
Observe the spheroid under an inverted brightfield microscope to detect changes in morphology.
Use fluorescence microscopy to observe optical reporters (GFP and RFP) with appropriate filter settings: GFP — 469 nm excitation, 525 nm emission; RFP — 559 nm excitation, 630 nm emission.
Irradiate the spheroid with NIR-light via LEDs emitting light at wavelengths of 670 to 710 nm for 2 J/cm².
Transfer the irradiated spheroid into a new hanging drop plate containing 50 µl of fresh culture media.
Incubate the spheroid in a humidified incubator at 37 °C and 5% carbon dioxide for 1 day.
Transfer the spheroid gently to a glass-bottomed dish with 100 µl of fresh culture media (phenol red free) using a sterile 200 µl pipette tip with the tip cut off.
Observe the spheroid with a fluorescence microscope 1 day after NIR-PIT using filter settings described in step 3.3.
Detect dead cells by adding propidium iodide to the media at a final concentration of 2 µg/ml.
Detect dead cells by observing loss of cytoplasmic GFP-fluorescence using a fluorescence microscope.
Repeat steps 3.1-3.6 if target cells are not completely eliminated.
